Morgan (sec): Heads up — NVD published CVE-2025-xxxxx for NVIDIA Unix display/driver stack. Appears to allow local privilege escalation via driver ioctl. link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-xxxxx
Aditya (infra): Thanks. Do we know affected driver versions?
Morgan (sec): Initial advisory says 525.x and 530.x branches, Linux kernel modules that expose pci device ioctls. Vendor bulletin also mentions CUDA compatibility matrix.
Sara (eng-ml): Which models + instances do we run on Dedicated and Private? If it's 530.x we might hit our DGX fleet and some GCE GPUs.
Liam (sre): Quick grep shows ~120 machines in prod have 530.41 and 530.56 packages. Staging mostly on 525.
Natalie (release): Any customer-facing impact? Is this remote exploit or local only?
Morgan (sec): Local only per vendor, requires unprivileged user to have access to /dev/nvidia* (typical for containerized inference). The attack is escalation to root from a container — HIGH for us.
Aditya (infra): Ok priority=high. We need to triage compatibility with our CUDA/cuDNN/NCCL pinned images before patching drivers. Patch candidates: vendor hotfix 530.67 and 525.90.
Sara (eng-ml): If we upgrade to 530.67, we must validate cuDNN 8.10 and CUDA 12.2 workloads. Some of our older models are pinned to CUDA 11.8 images.
Liam (sre): Suggested approach: 1) quick blocklist on user namespaces (restrict /dev access) 2) smoke patch on canary nodes with full perf tests 3) rollout with surge capacity.
Natalie (release): Can we sign drivers with our KMS or require driver packages to be verified at install-time? There's also concerns about package provenance for Private customers.
Aditya (infra): Driver packages are currently apt/rpm from vendor repos; we don't re-sign. For Private we inject our KMS-based verification hook for node bootstrap, but not for host-level driver updates.
Morgan (sec): Let's add a short-term mitigation: revoke container runtime access to /dev/nvidia* unless explicitly required. Add RBAC change: default gpu-access role -> no device nodes. That should buy time.
Sara (eng-ml): That will break everything unless we whitelist infra pipelines and model servers. We'll need a rollout plan.
Aditya (infra): I'll open a custodian policy: deny device access for non-whitelisted workloads. Also add audit logging to capture any attempts to access /dev/nvidia* during the mitigation window.
Liam (sre): For compatibility validation matrix: I propose permutations: [driver 525.90, 530.67] x [CUDA 11.8, 12.1, 12.2] x [cuDNN 8.7, 8.10] x [NCCL 2.14, 2.16]. Run 10 representative workloads (LLM token gen, embeddings, batching).
Sara (eng-ml): I'll run the ML perf suite — expect 6h per permutation on a single node. Need parallelization.
natalie (release): We'll need rollout gating checks: no regressions >5% latency, no OOMs, no failed init errors. Also verify model bitsafe endpoints.
deploy-bot: INFO: Created canary job gpu-driver-patch-canary-180500 on pool-1.
ops-runner: For canary, recommend 3 nodes across 2 AZs with mixed CUDA images. I'll provision.
Aditya (infra): Note: for Private customers, we must provide a signed patch bundle and HSM logs for compliance. Morgan, can you draft an audit statement requirement?
Morgan (sec): Yes — we need a signed release manifest, KMS verification step during bootstrap, and audit trail for who triggered each host patch. I'll draft. Also add requirement: kernel module signature verification enabled where supported.
Sara (eng-ml): One more: check GPU container runtimes (nvidia-container-toolkit) compatibility — sometimes driver bumps require runtime updates. I'll validate runtime v2.9 vs v2.10.
Liam (sre): Action items: Aditya will produce canary images + device whitelist policy (owner: Aditya). Sara runs perf/compat tests (owner: Sara). Morgan drafts audit/KMS requirements and RBAC change (owner: Morgan). Natalie coordinates customer comms and private bundles (owner: Natalie). Ops-runner provisions canary and monitors (owner: Ops-runner).
Aditya (infra): ETA: canary ready in ~3 hours. Sara: can you parallelize tests across 4 nodes?
Sara (eng-ml): Yes, will kick off after canary. Post results in this thread.
Morgan (sec): If canary shows no regression and runtime compatibility holds, plan to schedule off-peak staged rollout with automatic rollback on failure. Add post-rollout audit report. :thumbsup:
Natalie (release): I'll prepare a short customer bulletin for Dedicated/Private in case we need urgent patching.
Aditya (infra): FYI — I'll also add a pre-check script operators must run:
```
# verify driver
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader
# verify module signature
cat /sys/module/nvidia/version || echo "unsigned"
```
Liam (sre): Good. Keep me posted. If we see exploit attempts in logs, escalate to incident channel.
Morgan (sec): Agreed. I'll set a detection rule for anomalous ioctl patterns and alert to #incidents.
deploy-bot: INFO: Created ticket INFRA-4321 for driver patch rollout tracking.
Aditya (infra): Closing loop: will post canary logs and a short runbook for rollback here.
Sara (eng-ml): Canary started. Posting initial perf after 2 hours.
Morgan (sec): Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene here with canary outcome.
